does: Fries rolls or parcels of thin pastry in a layer of hot oil, seam side down first, turning them until they are evenly golden and crisp, then drains them on paper.

intro.what: Frying börek cooks thin-pastry rolls in a layer of hot oil until crisp and golden.
intro.why: It teaches how thin pastry crisps fast in hot oil and burns just as fast.

how: Heat oil in a frying pan to about the depth of a finger, until a scrap of pastry sizzles at once.
Lay the rolls in seam side down, so that the seam sets first and stays shut.
Fry a few at a time, turning them until golden on every side.
Lift them out onto paper to drain, and serve them warm.

cues.text: A brisk sizzle the moment a roll goes in.
An even, pale gold colour all round, with no dark ends.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is not hot, so that the pastry drinks oil and turns greasy.
mistakes.fix: Test with a scrap of pastry first.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, so that the oil cools and the rolls stick together.
mistakes.fix: Fry a few at a time.

quiz.question: Why put the rolls in seam side down?
choices: So the seam sets first and stays shut.
So they soak up less oil.
quiz.because: The seam sets in the hot oil and holds the roll closed.

quiz.question: How many rolls go in at once?
choices: A few, with room between them.
quiz.because: A crowded pan cools the oil and the rolls stick.

quiz.question: When is a roll done?
choices: When it is pale and soft.
When it is evenly golden and crisp all round.
quiz.because: Thin pastry is done once it is golden and crisp.

quiz.question: The rolls come out greasy. What should change?
choices: Heat the oil until a scrap sizzles at once.
quiz.because: Hot oil seals the pastry fast so it does not soak.

comes_after.why: The rolls are shaped and sealed before they meet the oil.

variant_of.differs: Rolls of thin pastry go seam side down into a deeper layer of oil and are turned until evenly golden. Only the pastry needs to crisp and the filling to melt.
